_note: Meal cards. Each is just a TITLE plus a list of search terms - the shopping list already turns a name into the best-scoring product that passes your filters and diet profile, so a meal needs no scoring logic of its own. Every term below was checked against the real catalog before being added; loose words resolve badly and the failures are not obvious. Three that were caught and fixed: 'butter' matched butter LETTUCE, 'yukon potatoes' matched instant mashed potato mix, and 'tortilla' matched tortilla CHIPS. Re-check with scripts/check_meals.py after any catalog change. `image` is a photo under the Unsplash License (see assets/meals/LICENSE.txt) - free for commercial use, no attribution required. Every candidate was VIEWED before being kept: one that looked plausible from its URL was a stack of books, another was pancakes rather than oats. To swap one, replace assets/meals/<id>.jpg. `spice` (mild / kick / hot) drives the dinner picker's spice question; set by hand 2026-10-03 from each recipe (hot sauce, chili, curry, sriracha = hot).
